translator.evidence: The Sundanese (Latin script; neutral everyday register) catalog is recorded as a complete original project localization contribution. The source fragment does not identify an individual translator, so no personal, human, or native-speaker identity is asserted. Updated 2026-09-28 with 69 original messages for change review, agent questions, permission rules, connectors, background runs, research progress and budgets. Placeholders and locale-specific plural forms are preserved; no upstream translated text was copied.

reviewer.evidence: All 12 family/shared slices were independently read for meaning, register, script, technical terms, and unintended English prose. An AST-based source review confirmed full key coverage, default-key order within every slice, placeholder multisets, and the locale’s CLDR plural-category set. The scaffold report was also used for untranslated-entry discovery and syntax parsing. No tests, builds, typechecks, or gates were run. Corrections: Translated the remaining English plural count labels and corrected “tool call” so it no longer reads as a telephone call. Clarified flow-connection and legend-scale wording, localized citation terminology, corrected the graph pin action, and translated color hue/opacity labels. Terminology uncertainties: Sundanese software terminology for “prompt”, “embedding”, “node”, “span”, “query”, and “spreadsheet” is less standardized; regional register preference should be checked by a native reviewer. Not claimed; this is an AI-assisted independent semantic review. Allowlist has 105 message paths with per-path rationales. Updated 2026-09-28: an independent AI-assisted review checked all 69 added messages for meaning, UI register, terminology and placeholders, and corrected the catalog before this snapshot. The research-source count was checked against the pinned CLDR categories, including locale-specific decimal and non-singular forms. The complete 1,384-key snapshot was checked for key coverage, value kinds, placeholders and exact-English message paths; only individually justified new cognates, loanwords and technical names were retained. This increment does not claim a new linguistic review of all older messages, human review or native-speaker certification.
